# Claims and their evidence

Every statement below is backed by evidence checked in CI, or is explicitly marked as not delivered. Status vocabulary: PROVEN, PROVEN-CAVEAT, IN-SAMPLE, SIMULATED, NOT-DELIVERED, OWNER-PENDING, RETRACTED.

| ID | Claim | Status | Reservation |
|---|---|---|---|
| C-007 | The intent of a request is written (write-ahead log, fsync) before the provider is called; at boot, entries left open are closed. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | There is no explicit COMMIT entry yet; a stream open at a crash is closed as STREAM_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; durability across a sudden power loss is not demonstrated on hardware. |
| C-009 | Offline verifiers with no dependency on QODIQA code exist in JavaScript and Python, with published test vectors. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | To rely on a verification independently of the instance, the public keys must come from a source other than that instance. |
| C-017 | Adapters exist for Azure OpenAI and AWS Bedrock. | SIMULATED | Verified only with simulated transport; no calls to the real hosted services have been made. |
| C-020 | Logs are sanitized automatically (PII, tokens). Automatic redaction of AI prompt content is not available. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | Log sanitization only; no data-loss-prevention on prompts or responses. |
| C-021 | Technical features that support GDPR work are present: data-subject requests, lawful basis recording and retention. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | These are technical controls, not a certification or a legal assessment. |

| C-027 | SDKs for TypeScript, Python, Go and Java are available in the repository; each covers every operation of the API contract through generated descriptor tables, and verifies artifacts offline. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | Not published to any registry. The generated operation layer is verified against the contract, not exercised operation by operation against a live gateway; the sign, verify, chat, generic-call and error-mapping paths were run against an installed gateway. |
| C-030 | Kustomize, Helm, Terraform, Docker Compose and systemd deployment assets exist, and backup and restore are documented. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | Kubernetes and the Helm chart were exercised only on local kind clusters in the development profile; the production profile (TLS to PostgreSQL and Redis, a shared keystore volume, NetworkPolicy enforcement) was rendered and validated, not run on a real cluster. Incremental backup and point-in-time recovery are not supported. |
| C-031 | A protocol-V2 artifact binds the request's query string and the headers the issuer chose, in addition to the method, path and body; changing any of them makes the request fail with REQUEST_MISMATCH. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | Protocol V2 issuance is off by default (QODIQA_PROTOCOL_V2_ISSUE); V1 artifacts keep binding method, path and body only. A raw + or ; in a bound query is refused (use %20, %2B, %3B). |
| C-032 | A decision can come with a signed receipt that anyone can verify offline with the gateway's public transparency keys; the receipt proves the gateway recorded the decision, not that the decision was correct. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | Present only when the audit entry and the transparency leaf are persisted (otherwise absent); streaming responses carry no receipt yet; retrieval by request id works for a bounded window (default one hour). |
| C-034 | An operator can revoke a single signed artifact before it is used; a revoked artifact is refused before its nonce is consumed. | PROVEN | — |
| C-035 | With audit schema v8 enabled, every request whose provider executed ends with a COMMIT audit entry written after the response: the exact number of output bytes delivered, the hash of the delivered text and how the delivery ended (complete, client disconnected, timeout, cancelled, error); a stream that stops half-way commits the bytes that did reach the client. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | Audit schema v8 is off by default (owner decision), so no COMMIT is written until it is enabled; a request whose process dies between its DECISION and its COMMIT gets a COMMIT with completionStatus OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and 0 bytes (unknown) written by the next boot, not the true delivery record; a COMMIT refused by the audit store is queued durably. |
| C-038 | With two or more co-signing witnesses configured, an audit checkpoint is exported as anchored only when at least two cosignatures verify under the trusted witness keys; each witness keeps its own key and its own append-only log and refuses rollback, equivocation and forks, so one compromised or unreachable witness can neither anchor a checkpoint alone nor make the other cosign a different head. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | The witnesses run as separate processes with their own keys in the tests; whether two witnesses are operated by independent parties is a deployment fact (owner-level, FO.10), not something the software can check. With fewer than two witnesses configured the quorum is one. |
| C-039 | Audit history can be exported as a sealed archive without deleting anything: the chain segment up to a signed checkpoint, the checkpoint, a manifest of file hashes and a seal signed by the audit-checkpoint key, marked in an append-only hash-chained index and verifiable offline years later; ENFORCEMENT audit events are never deleted automatically, and removing history from the hot store remains an operator-run command that archives and verifies first. | PROVEN-CAVEAT | The exporter covers the file chain; PostgreSQL-authoritative deployments rely on the database backup and the prune archive; moving archives to cold storage and verifying them on a schedule are operator steps. |
